messages:
Maria (oncall): quick heads-up — I'm handing off in ~20m (leaving primary at 23:30 UTC). We saw a rise in 5xx on /api/generate starting ~22:50 UTC. Small subset of q8 model variants throwing errors, affecting some Dedicated pinned pools. Thinking we should temporarily relax the SLO alert to cut paging noise while we triage.
Kevin: how bad is "rise"? Is it a full outage for any customer?
Maria (oncall): not full outage. Baseline 5xx ~0.3%, peaked at ~1.9% over 30m. Tail latency stable. Majority of traffic fine; a few large clients with pinned q8 pools saw retries. Hosted fallback working for most. No SLA breach yet but noise and repeated pages.
incident-bot: Incident 2026-03-14-1955 opened: route=/api/generate elevated 5xx. Paging eng-oncall primary/secondary. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/api-generate-5xx
AJ: I'll be primary until 02:00 UTC, can run mitigation. Maria, do you want me to request an alert threshold change so we don't get flooded during handoff?
Maria (oncall): yes please. Proposal: temporarily bump SLO-error alert from 0.5% -> 2.5% for 45m, add 5m suppression for repeat pages, and route non-sev incidents to Slack-only (no pager) during this window. Example alert rule patch:

```
alert: Generate5xxSpike
expr: sum(rate(http_requests_total{route="/api/generate",code=~"5.."}[5m]))
/ sum(rate(http_requests_total{route="/api/generate"}[5m])) > 0.025
for: 1m
annotations:
  severity: warning
  runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/api-generate-5xx
```
Olga: agree. Also recommend a short routing fallback: if 5xx > 1% for 2m, shift q8 traffic to q4-compatible pools gradually (canary -> 20% -> 40%). That avoids full rollback.
Kevin: I can apply the alert change. AJ focus on mitigation. Use infra job: `./infra/ops alter-alert Generate5xxSpike --threshold 0.025 --suppression 300s` (infra-ops role required).
AJ: I'll run the routing canary and monitor. Maria, leave any handoff notes in the shift log.
Kevin: kicking off alter-alert job now.
Kevin: prow: alter-alert job started
Kevin: prow: alter-alert job succeeded — new threshold 2.5%, suppression 300s
Maria (oncall): noted in handoff: primary -> AJ at 23:30 UTC, Samir secondary but Samir has partial PTO at 00:30-06:00 UTC. Samir, can you extend coverage to 01:30 UTC tonight?
Samir: I can extend to 01:30 UTC. After that I need to drop. If things look bad at 01:15 I'll fully wake.
Olga: mitigation update: canary routing applied to q4 pool, canary error rate dropped to baseline. Rolling to 20% now.
AJ: can we push to 40% traffic-split away from q8 for the next 30m while watching metrics?
Maria (oncall): follow runbook step 4. Command to modify routing split:

```
redwoodctl route modify --service api-gen --split \"q8:0.6,q4:0.4\" --reason \"swing-shift emergency\"
```
AJ: applying traffic-split now, monitoring dashboards.
AJ: traffic-split applied. Error rate back to ~0.45% within 4m. No additional pages. I'll hold primary until 02:00 UTC and watch for 30m post-rollback.
Kevin: noted. I'll add a runbook entry documenting the temporary alert override and rollback plan.
Maria (oncall): customer impact blurb for incident ticket: approx 2% of gen requests experienced 5xx between 22:50-23:10 UTC. Most clients retried; hosted fallback mitigated broad impact. No SLA violation detected during window. Creating follow-up: eng-sre to do model-variant healthcheck.
sre-bot: Post-incident task created: SRE-2026-487 — model-variant stability analysis. Assignee: eng-sre
AJ: I'll keep an eye until 02:00 UTC. Samir covers until 01:30 UTC. If error rate rebounds we revert routing and reopen paging.
Maria (oncall): handoff complete. Shift log note: temp SLO threshold 0.5% -> 2.5% from 23:20-00:05 UTC, traffic-split q4 applied at 23:40 UTC, monitoring and rollback plan in place. :white_check_mark:
Samir: calendar updated to show partial coverage. :thumbsup:
Kevin: added follow-up for oncall retro to review q8->q4 fallback behavior and possible long-term fix.
incident-bot: Incident 2026-03-14-1955 status: mitigated — paging suppressed per alert override, routing fallback active, monitoring ongoing.
